title: Compression tools
intro: Work from the module directory. Tools: **`gzip`** / **`gunzip`**, **`bzip2`**, **`zip`** / **`unzip`**. Do not overwrite the committed fixture files.

questions.prompt: Report the byte sizes of **`corpus.txt`** (uncompressed) and **`corpus.txt.gz`** (compressed) as `U,C` — uncompressed first, compressed second, comma-separated with no spaces.
What is the first line of **`corpus.txt.gz`** when decompressed?
Test the integrity of **`corpus.txt.gz`** without decompressing it to a file. What exit code indicates the archive is intact?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
gzip -t corpus.txt.gz; echo $?
```

`gzip -t` verifies the checksum; exit code `0` means the archive is not corrupted.

questions.prompt: How many lines does **`corpus.txt.bz2`** contain when decompressed?
Test the integrity of **`m14.zip`**. What exit code indicates success?
How many bytes does **`corpus.txt.gz`** expand to when fully decompressed?
Compare the sizes of **`corpus.txt.gz`** and **`corpus.txt.bz2`**. Which format produced the smaller file for this corpus?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
wc -c corpus.txt.gz corpus.txt.bz2
```

`corpus.txt.gz` is 50 bytes vs `corpus.txt.bz2` at 70 bytes — gzip wins on this highly repetitive corpus.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the file stored inside **`m14.zip`**?
Decompress **`corpus.txt.gz`** to `work/corpus_restored.txt`. Compare it byte-for-byte with the original **`corpus.txt`**. What exit code does the comparison return when files are identical?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
mkdir -p work
gzip -dc corpus.txt.gz > work/corpus_restored.txt
cmp corpus.txt work/corpus_restored.txt; echo $?
```

`cmp` exits `0` if the files match byte-for-byte.

questions.prompt: What are the byte sizes of the two compressed fixture files in this module — **`corpus.txt.gz`** and **`corpus.txt.bz2`** — listed from smallest to largest as `S,L`?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
wc -c corpus.txt.gz corpus.txt.bz2 | sort -n | head -2
```

`corpus.txt.gz` = 50 bytes, `corpus.txt.bz2` = 70 bytes.

questions.prompt: `secret.zip` is in the module directory. It contains a compressed file. Decompress the full chain — zip layer first, then the inner compression — and read the flag. What does it contain?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
unzip -p secret.zip inner.txt.bz2 | bzip2 -dc
```

`unzip -p` sends the member to stdout without creating files; piping into `bzip2 -dc` decompresses the second layer in one pass.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes
- Compress and decompress with `gzip` / `gunzip` / `zcat`; know `pigz` for parallel gzip.
- Use `zip` / `unzip` for Windows-friendly bundles and selective extract.
- Optionally use `zstd` levels and dictionary training (mention only).
- Chain `xz` / `lz4` where installed for extreme ratios vs speed trade-offs.

## Scope

**In scope:** single-file and stream compressors commonly found on servers. **Out of scope:** `rar` licensing; proprietary codecs.
